letters.name: a
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'a' in English 'father' — open and clear. Slovak a is short and crisp, never drawn out.

letters.name: dlhé a (long a)
letters.memoryTrick: A longer, stretched version of 'a' — like the 'a' in English 'car' but held twice as long. The acute accent means 'hold it!'

letters.name: a s dvoma bodkami (a with two dots)
letters.memoryTrick: Pronounced between 'a' and 'e' — like the 'e' in English 'bet' with a slight 'a' color. In modern Slovak, often sounds just like 'e'.

letters.name: bé
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 'b' — a soft, voiced 'buh' sound made with both lips. No tricks needed.

letters.name: cé
letters.memoryTrick: Always like 'ts' in English 'cats' — never soft like 'city'. Think of the zippy 'ts' sound and you've got it every time.

letters.name: čé
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ch' in English 'chocolate' or 'church'. The little hook (caron/háčik) turns a plain 'ts' into a 'ch' — think of it as 'c with a cherry on top.'

letters.name: dé
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'd' in 'dog' — a voiced tap of the tongue behind the upper teeth. No surprises here.

letters.name: ďé
letters.memoryTrick: A soft 'd' — say 'd' but press the middle of your tongue up toward your palate, like the 'd' in British English 'duke' or 'during.' The háčik softens it.

letters.name: dzé
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ds' in English 'beds' or 'kids' — a voiced 'ts' sound. It's one letter in Slovak even though it looks like two, and sounds like a buzzing bee moving from 'd' to 'z.'

letters.name: džé
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'j' in English 'jump' or 'dge' in 'bridge.' The háčik turns dz into a juicy 'j' sound — think of it as the sound of a DJ scratching a record.

letters.name: e
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'e' in English 'bet' or 'let' — short, open, and crisp. Never silent at the end of words like in English.

letters.name: dlhé e (long e)
letters.memoryTrick: A longer, more open 'e' — like the 'ai' in English 'air' but held steady and longer. The acute accent stretches the sound.

letters.name: ef
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 'f' — a soft breath between your upper teeth and lower lip. Think of gently blowing out a candle.

letters.name: gé
letters.memoryTrick: Always a hard 'g' like in English 'go' or 'garden' — never soft like 'giraffe.' Slovak g is always tough.

letters.name: há
letters.memoryTrick: A voiced 'h' — like the 'h' in English 'behind' or 'ahead,' where your vocal cords buzz a little. Softer and warmer than the English breathy 'h' at the start of 'hat.'

letters.name: chá
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ch' in Scottish 'loch' or German 'Bach' — a scratchy sound made at the back of your throat. It's a single letter in Slovak, filed after 'h' in the dictionary.

letters.name: i
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'i' in English 'bit' or 'sit' — short and relaxed. Not like 'eye' or 'ee' — keep it quick and soft.

letters.name: dlhé i (long i)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ee' in English 'see' or 'bee' — a long, clear 'ee' held twice as long as short i. The acute accent stretches it out.

letters.name: jé
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'y' in English 'yes' or 'yellow' — a quick glide, never like English 'j' in 'jump.' Slovak j is always a 'y' sound.

letters.name: ká
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'k' in English 'kite' or 'skip' — crisp and unaspirated (no puff of air). Keep it clean and sharp.

letters.name: el
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'l' in English 'let' or 'lamp' — a clear, light 'l' made with the tip of the tongue behind the upper teeth.

letters.name: dlhé el (long l)
letters.memoryTrick: A long, syllabic 'l' — hold the 'l' sound for twice as long, like you're humming on an 'l'. Rare, appearing in only a few words. Think of it as 'lll' held steady.

letters.name: eľ
letters.memoryTrick: A soft, palatal 'l' — like 'lli' in English 'million' or the 'gli' in Italian 'figlio.' Press the middle of your tongue to your palate while saying 'l.'

letters.name: em
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'm' in English 'mother' — a hum made with both lips together. Warm and straightforward.

letters.name: en
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'n' in English 'no' or 'net' — tongue tip behind upper teeth. Clean and simple.

letters.name: eň
letters.memoryTrick: A soft, palatal 'n' — like 'ni' in English 'onion' or the Spanish 'ñ' in 'señor.' Press the middle of your tongue to your palate. Slovak ň is the same sound as Spanish ñ.

letters.name: o
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'o' in English 'or' or 'door' — a rounded, open sound. Never like 'oh' in 'go.' Keep it short and open.

letters.name: dlhé o (long o)
letters.memoryTrick: A longer, stretched 'o' — like the 'aw' in English 'law' held steady. The acute accent means 'keep this o going.' Mostly appears in loanwords.

letters.name: ô (o s vokáňom)
letters.memoryTrick: A unique Slovak diphthong — like 'wo' in English 'won't' or 'uo' blended together. Start with 'u' as in 'put' and glide to 'o.' The circumflex (vokáň) creates this special sound.

letters.name: pé
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'p' in English 'pen' or 'spot' — crisp and unaspirated (no puff of air). Keep it clean, almost like a softer 'p.'

letters.name: kvé
letters.memoryTrick: Only in foreign words — pronounced like 'k.' Always followed by 'u' as in 'kv-'. Slovak prefers native spelling without q.

letters.name: er
letters.memoryTrick: A rolled, trilled 'r' — like the 'rr' in Spanish 'perro.' Tap your tongue rapidly against the roof of your mouth, just behind your teeth. Practice with 'brr, it's cold!'

letters.name: dlhé er (long r)
letters.memoryTrick: A long, syllabic rolled 'r' — hold the trill for twice as long. Very rare. Think of a cat purring for an extra beat: 'rrrrr.'

letters.name: es
letters.memoryTrick: Always a crisp 's' like in English 'sun' or 'hiss' — never voiced like 'z.' Slovak s never sounds like 'z' in 'rose.'

letters.name: eš
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'sh' in English 'shoe' or 'fish.' The háčik adds a hushing quality to plain 's.' Think of someone going 'shhh!' — that's š.

letters.name: té
letters.memoryTrick: Like 't' in English 'stop' or 'top' — crisp and unaspirated. Keep it clean without the puff of air English speakers add.

letters.name: ťé
letters.memoryTrick: A soft 't' — like the 't' in British English 'tune' or 'Tuesday.' Press the middle of your tongue to your palate. The háčik makes it gentle and palatal.

letters.name: u
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'oo' in English 'book' or 'put' — a short, rounded vowel made with pursed lips. Not like 'you' or 'uh.'

letters.name: dlhé u (long u)
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'oo' in English 'moon' or 'food' — a long, clear 'oo' held twice as long as short u. Purse your lips and let it ring.

letters.name: vé
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'v' in English 'voice' or 'very' — a soft buzz between your lower lip and upper teeth. Never silent.

letters.name: dvojité vé (double v)
letters.memoryTrick: Only in foreign words — pronounced the same as Slovak 'v.' Think of it as a fancy 'v' for borrowed words. Slovak doesn't need it natively.

letters.name: iks
letters.memoryTrick: Only in foreign words — pronounced 'ks.' Always sounds like the 'x' in English 'box' or 'taxi.' Native Slovak words don't use x.

letters.name: ypsilon
letters.memoryTrick: In Slovak, 'y' sounds exactly the same as 'i' — both are /ɪ/. The difference is historical and affects spelling rules (hard vs. soft consonants). Don't worry about the sound; just memorize which words use y.

letters.name: dlhý ypsilon (long y)
letters.memoryTrick: A long 'y' — sounds exactly like long í (/iː/). Like 'ee' in English 'see.' The acute accent stretches the sound, but the y vs. í distinction is purely about spelling rules.

letters.name: zet
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'z' in English 'zebra' or 'buzz' — a voiced buzz. Always voiced, never like 'ts.' Think of a bee: 'zzzz.'

letters.name: žet
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 's' in English 'pleasure' or 'measure,' or the 'zh' sound in 'Dr. Zhivago.' A buzzy, humming 'sh.' The háčik adds voice to a plain 'sh.'
